description: An eight-panel composite of micrographs of 800 °C-tempered Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels, arranged as two rows of four. The upper row is optical microscope micrographs and the lower row is secondary electron (SEM) images, both ordered left to right as (a) 9Al-10Mn-1C, (b) 12Al-10Mn-1C, (c) 12Al-20Mn-1C and (d) 12Al-30Mn-1C. The optical panels show progressively more heterogeneous structures: (a) equiaxed grains crossed by faint horizontal bands, (b) a nearly featureless weakly banded surface, (c) dark elongated stringers/bands lying in a lighter matrix, and (d) strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several with internal transformation. The SEM panels carry printed acquisition data — "20kV X2,500 10µm" for (a), (c), (d) and "20kV X5,000 5µm" for (b). SEM (a) and (b) resolve fine lamellar κ-carbide + ferrite colonies; (c) shows lamellae emanating from a boundary next to a finely modulated region; (d) shows rounded, droplet-like lighter regions in a darker matrix. Taken together the group visualises the transition from cellular transformation (a–c) toward spinodal decomposition (d). Optical scale-bar text is unreadable at the supplied resolution.

observations.observation: The group is a composite: the top row is optical microscope micrographs and the bottom row is secondary electron (SEM) images, matched column-wise to four alloys.
The images are labelled (a) 9Al-10Mn-1C, (b) 12Al-10Mn-1C, (c) 12Al-20Mn-1C and (d) 12Al-30Mn-1C, all from 800 °C-tempered alloys.
SEM acquisition data are printed on each lower-row panel: '20kV X2,500 10µm' for (a), (c) and (d), and '20kV X5,000 5µm' for (b).
Optical micrograph (c) shows dark, elongated stringers/bands within a lighter matrix, differing from the more uniform banding of (a) and (b).
Optical micrograph (d) shows strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several of which display internal transformation, distinguishing it from panels (a)-(c).
SEM panel (b) resolves dense fine κ-carbide/ferrite lamellae at higher magnification (X5,000), consistent with coarse lamellar colonies.
SEM panel (c) shows lamellar cells nucleated at a boundary together with a smoother, finely modulated adjacent region.
SEM panel (d) shows rounded, droplet-like light regions dispersed in a darker matrix, the morphology expected of spinodal decomposition.
The text states that only alloys tempered at 800 °C underwent cellular transformation and/or spinodal decomposition.
The text states that for high Al and C with medium Mn, austenite underwent both spinodal decomposition and cellular transformation, giving κ + α + γ lamellar structures.
The text states that at 12Al-10Mn-1C austenite underwent full cellular transformation into κ-carbide coarse lamellae with high inter-lamellar spacing.
The text states that increasing manganese to high content fully spinodally decomposed the austenite grains, linked to the microstructure of panel (d).
The text states that spinodal decomposition contributes to increasing the hardness level of the alloy.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of 800 °C-tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C: equiaxed grains crossed by faint horizontal banded/lamellar features; scale bar present but its text is illegible.
Optical micrograph of 800 °C-tempered 12Al-10Mn-1C: nearly featureless, weakly banded surface with little optical contrast; scale-bar text illegible.
Optical micrograph of 800 °C-tempered 12Al-20Mn-1C: dark, elongated stringers/bands lying in a lighter matrix; scale-bar text illegible.
Optical micrograph of 800 °C-tempered 12Al-30Mn-1C: strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several showing internal transformation/banding; scale-bar text illegible.
Secondary electron image, 20kV X2,500, 10 µm scale bar, of 9Al-10Mn-1C: a region of parallel lamellar κ-carbide + ferrite structure beside a smoother matrix grain.
Secondary electron image, 20kV X5,000, 5 µm scale bar, of 12Al-10Mn-1C: dense fine lamellar structure typical of full cellular transformation, over a large fraction of the field.
Secondary electron image, 20kV X2,500, 10 µm scale bar, of 12Al-20Mn-1C: lamellar cells emanating from a boundary at the top, next to a smoother, finely modulated region.
Secondary electron image, 20kV X2,500, 10 µm scale bar, of 12Al-30Mn-1C: rounded, droplet-like light regions in a darker matrix, consistent with spinodal decomposition.
